summary: At dawn in his brush hut by the sea, the pearl diver Kino feels content, until a scorpion stings his baby son, Coyotito. The family begs the town doctor for help, but he refuses to treat a poor native family.
details: Kino wakes before dawn in his brush house near the beach, beside his wife, Juana, and their baby, Coyotito, who sleeps in a hanging box. In his head he hears music his people have passed down: a calm, whole Song of the Family. Juana makes corn cakes and the morning feels complete.

Then a scorpion creeps down the rope of Coyotito’s box. Kino hears a darker music, the Song of Evil, and moves slowly to catch it, but the baby laughs and shakes the rope, and the scorpion falls and stings him on the shoulder. Kino crushes the scorpion. Juana sucks out what poison she can, the neighbours, among them Kino’s older brother Juan Tomás and his wife Apolonia, crowd into the doorway, and Juana demands the doctor, who has never come to their poor quarter.

The family walks into town, followed by curious neighbours and the beggars from the church steps. The doctor belongs to the race that conquered Kino’s people centuries ago, Kino addresses the doctor’s servant, one of his own people, in their old language, but the servant will not answer in it. Told that Kino has only a few small, misshapen pearls to pay with, the doctor sends word that he is out. Humiliated, Kino strikes the gate with his fist and cuts his knuckles open.

summary: Kino dives for oysters while Juana treats Coyotito with a seaweed poultice and prays for luck. Kino finds a huge oyster, and inside it the greatest pearl anyone has ever seen.
details: The family goes down to the shore and Kino’s canoe, his most valuable possession, handed down from his grandfather. Juana makes a poultice of brown seaweed for Coyotito’s swollen shoulder, a remedy that may be as good as the doctor’s, though no one values it because it costs nothing.

Out over the oyster bed, Kino dives with a stone and a basket, hearing the Song of the Pearl That Might Be. Juana prays, not quite out loud, that he will find a pearl to pay the doctor. Near the end of his dive he spots one large oyster lying apart from the rest and brings it up.

When he pries open the big oyster, he finds a pearl the size of a gull’s egg, perfectly shaped and glowing: the Pearl of the World. Juana sees that the swelling on Coyotito’s shoulder is going down. Kino throws back his head and howls, and the other canoes race toward him.

summary: News of the pearl stirs up the whole town. Kino dreams aloud of a church wedding, new clothes, a rifle and schooling for Coyotito. The doctor suddenly comes to treat the baby, and that night someone breaks in to steal the pearl.
details: Before Kino is even home, the town knows about the pearl, and everyone starts to want something from it: the priest thinks of church repairs, the shopkeepers of goods to sell, the beggars of alms, the pearl buyers of profit. The doctor tells a patient that the baby with the scorpion sting is his client. Kino has become everyone’s enemy without knowing it.

In his hut, surrounded by neighbours and his brother, Juan Tomás, Kino says what the pearl will buy: a proper church wedding with Juana, new clothes, a rifle, and above all school for Coyotito, so he can read and know things. The neighbours are startled by his boldness. The priest visits to remind Kino to give thanks for his treasure and to pray for guidance.

The doctor arrives with his servant, claims scorpion poison can strike later, and gives Coyotito a white powder. Within the hour the baby falls violently ill, and the doctor returns to “cure” him; Kino suspects a trick. When the doctor asks about the pearl, Kino’s glance gives away where it is hidden, so afterwards he digs it up and hides it somewhere new.

That night someone creeps into the hut. Kino fights the intruder in the dark, and is struck on the head as the attacker escapes. Juana begs him to destroy the pearl or throw it back into the sea, saying it will destroy them. Kino refuses: this is their one chance, and he means to fight for it.

summary: Kino takes the pearl to the buyers, who pretend to compete but offer him a fraction of its worth. He refuses and decides to sell in the capital. Juan Tomás warns him of the danger, and that night Kino is attacked again.
details: The whole neighbourhood follows Kino, Juana and Coyotito to the pearl buyers’ street. The buyers appear to be rivals, but the town suspects they all work for a single man. The first buyer, who rolls a coin across his knuckles as he talks, examines the pearl and dismisses it as a curiosity too large to be valuable, offering a thousand pesos.

Kino is outraged: he knows it is worth fifty thousand. The other buyers are called in one by one, and each disparages the pearl and offers less or nothing; the first buyer then raises his offer to fifteen hundred. Sensing a trap, Kino snatches it back and announces that he will go to the capital to sell it himself.

That evening Juan Tomás reminds him of men who once tried to sell their pearls in the capital and were never heard of again. Kino has defied the whole system of the town, and he is afraid, but determined. That night, outside the hut, he is attacked in the dark again. He slashes out with his knife and drives the attackers off, but is left bleeding. Juana begs him again to give up the pearl; Kino insists that he is a man and will go to the capital.

summary: Juana tries to throw the pearl into the sea and Kino beats her. Attacked once more, Kino kills a man. His canoe is smashed and his house burned, and the family hides with Juan Tomás before fleeing north.
details: In the night Juana takes the pearl and slips down to the shore to throw it into the sea. Kino catches her, tears it from her hand, strikes her in the face and kicks her. She watches him without anger: she understands that the pearl has driven him half mad.

Walking back, Kino is attacked by several men. Juana, recovering, finds the pearl lying on the path, and then sees Kino struggling to his feet beside a dead man with a knife wound in his throat. Kino has killed someone, and they must flee.

Juana runs for Coyotito while Kino goes to prepare the canoe, but someone has smashed a hole in its bottom: a crime worse than killing a man, Kino feels. Then the hut bursts into flames. With nowhere else to go, the family hides in Juan Tomás’s house, where his wife, Apolonia, is mourning them as dead. Juan Tomás keeps them hidden all day and gathers supplies.
Juan Tomás asks whether Kino should get rid of the pearl, but Kino says the pearl has become his soul. When darkness falls, Kino, Juana and Coyotito set out north toward the capital.

summary: Fleeing north, the family is hunted by trackers. In the mountains Kino attacks them at night, but a rifle shot kills Coyotito. Kino and Juana walk back to town, and Kino throws the pearl into the sea.
details: They travel by night and hide by day. Kino finds himself hoping again, picturing the future the pearl will bring. But when he looks back from a hiding place, he sees trackers: two men on foot reading the ground, and a horseman with a rifle, following their trail.

Kino tries to hide their tracks and they climb into the mountains, toward a pool of water among high rocks with small caves above it. Juana and Coyotito hide in a cave, but the trackers come and make camp beside the pool. Kino decides he must attack them before dawn, while the rifleman dozes.

He strips off his white clothes so they won’t show in the dark and creeps down. Just as he is ready, Coyotito cries out in the cave. One tracker thinks it is a coyote pup, and the rifleman fires toward the sound. Kino leaps on them and kills all three men, seizing the rifle. Then he hears Juana’s keening from the cave: the shot has killed Coyotito.

Late the next afternoon, Kino and Juana walk back into the town side by side, Kino carrying the rifle and Juana carrying the bundle of her dead child in her shawl. People step aside in silence. At the water’s edge, Kino offers the pearl to Juana, but she will not take it and leaves it to him. He throws it as far as he can, and it sinks to the bottom of the sea.
